scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tappa is a traditional folk dance of the Magar community, an indigenous group in Nepal.
It is most prominently practiced in the Dang District within the Rapti Zone.
The dance's history is tied to the local use of the pappa drum, though specific dates of origin are not recorded in the sources.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance follows a linear progression of speed.
It begins at a slow tempo and gradually accelerates.
Dancers must synchronize their movements with the beats of the pappa hand drum, reaching a high-speed conclusion as the drummer increases the tempo.
Watch for Pappa synchronization.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary instrument is the pappa, a local hand drum.
The rhythm of this drum drives the entire performance and is the source of the dance's name, Tappa.
Listen for the pappa (hand drum).
The tempo sits around 70 beats a minute.

The sound is dominated by the percussive strikes of the pappa hand drum. It begins with spaced, resonant beats that gradually compress into a rapid, driving pulse as the performance reaches its conclusion.
